note: Rough hand-built US repair-cost ranges for triage only. Not quotes. Real prices vary a lot by region, access and hidden damage.

crack.name: Crack
crack.cause: Usually settling or seasonal movement in plaster or drywall. Wide, long or growing cracks can point to structural movement.
crack.action: Fill and repaint small cracks. Have a structural engineer look at cracks wider than about 3 mm or longer than a metre.

stairstep_crack.name: Stair-step crack
stairstep_crack.cause: A zig-zag crack that follows mortar joints. It often means the foundation is settling unevenly.
stairstep_crack.action: Get a structural engineer or foundation specialist to assess it before making an offer.

mold.name: Mold
mold.cause: Persistent moisture: a leak, condensation or poor ventilation. It keeps coming back until the moisture source is fixed.
mold.action: Find and fix the moisture source, then clean or remove the affected material. Large areas need professional remediation.

peeling_paint.name: Peeling paint
peeling_paint.cause: Moisture behind the paint, poor surface preparation or age. In homes built before 1978 old paint may contain lead.
peeling_paint.action: Scrape, prime and repaint. Check for a moisture source, and test for lead in older homes before sanding.

water_seepage.name: Water stain / seepage
water_seepage.cause: Water getting in from a roof or plumbing leak, or seeping through a wall. A stain may be old and dry, or still active.
water_seepage.action: Trace the source and check whether it is still wet. Fix the leak first, then replace damaged material and repaint.

damaged_tile.name: Damaged tile
damaged_tile.cause: Impact, movement in the surface underneath, or water getting behind the tiles.
damaged_tile.action: Replace the cracked tiles and regrout. Check that water has not reached the wall or floor behind them.
